sections.heading: What Is Tempered Glass and Why Does It Matter?
sections.body: Tempered glass is a type of safety glass that has been heat-treated to increase its strength compared to standard glass. When broken, it shatters into small, rounded fragments rather than sharp, jagged shards, significantly reducing the risk of injury. This characteristic makes it a preferred choice for applications where people are likely to be near glass surfaces, such as entry doors, sidelights, shower enclosures, storefronts, and large window openings. In busy commercial corridors like those found near the Annandale area's retail and office strips, and in residential neighborhoods throughout the region, tempered glass offers a meaningful safety advantage over ordinary annealed glass. Understanding the difference between glass types helps property managers and homeowners make informed decisions when a replacement is needed. Our team can walk you through the right options based on your specific application, helping you choose glass that performs well for years to come.

faq.q: How do I know if my existing glass is tempered or standard glass?
faq.a: Tempered glass often has a small etched or printed label in one of its corners indicating that it is safety glass. It may also have a slight distortion visible when viewed at an angle due to the tempering process. If you are unsure, our technicians can help identify the glass type during an assessment and advise you on the best replacement option.
